battle.name: 克里米亞戰爭
battle.theater: 克里米亞半島與多瑙河下游
battle.brief: 一八五三年十月俄羅斯向鄂圖曼宣戰，英法聯手參戰，一八五四年聯軍登陸克里米亞半島，包圍塞瓦斯托波爾三百四十九日。本卡線膛砲是聯軍野戰與攻城嘅骨幹火力：阿爾馬河、因克曼兩役嘅砲戰，圍城線上嘅遠程轟擊同馬拉霍夫壘強攻，都靠佢喺射程上壓過城牆同砲壘。

kit.name: 線膛砲
kit.history: 線膛讓同樣的藥量走得更遠。砲兵第一次可以在射程上贏步兵。

countries: 交戰是兩大集團。俄羅斯帝國一方：皇帝尼古拉一世自一八五三年執政，一八五五年三月二日病逝後由亞歷山大二世接位；克里米亞的俄軍由陸軍元帥米哈伊爾·沃羅佐夫全權統率，多瑙河戰線先由維特根斯坦公爵指揮，同年二月改由康斯坦丁尼古拉耶維奇大公接掌，黑海艦隊由老將帕維爾·納希莫夫以亞速號一類帆布快艇編成的分隊作戰。聯盟一方是四國：英國由維克多利亞女王在位，陸軍總司令為拉格倫公爵；法國由拿破崙三世坐鎮，陸軍由麥克馬洪元帥率領，海軍由帕累托-布律埃爾上將指揮分艦隊駛入黑海；鄂圖曼帝國以蘇丹阿卜杜勒-哈米德一世當國，塞拉凱爾穆罕默德·艾敏·阿里帕夏掌軍政，克里米亞的鄂軍由穆斯塔法·菲茲·恰克馬克率領；撒丁王國於一八五五年參戰，維克多·伊曼紐爾二世派出拉·馬爾莫拉元帥率領約一萬五千人的遠征軍。奧地利與普魯士官方中立，但加利西亞有數千志願者以個人身份加入聯軍。戰區分三條：多瑙河戰線、高加索戰線、克里米亞主戰區。
countriesEn: The conflict pitted two blocs against each other. On the Russian side Emperor Nicholas I reigned from 1853 and died on 2 March 1855, when his son Alexander II took over; the Russian army in the Crimea was under the supreme command of Field Marshal Mikhail Vorontsov; the Danube front was led at first by Prince Wittgenstein and from February 1855 by Grand Duke Konstantin Nikolaevich; and the Black Sea squadron was fought by the veteran admiral Pavel Nakhimov with a division of steam corvettes such as the Azov. The coalition was made up of four states. Britain was under Queen Victoria with Lord Raglan as commander in chief; France was under Napoleon III, with Marshal MacMahon leading the French corps and Admiral de Parseval-Parseval commanding the naval division that sailed into the Black Sea; the Ottoman Empire was ruled by Sultan Abdülmecid I, with Serasker Mehmed Emin Ali Pasha at the head of the government and Mustafa Fevzi Çakmak commanding the Ottoman troops in the Crimea; and the Kingdom of Sardinia joined in 1855, sending roughly fifteen thousand men under General Alfonso La Marmora at the wish of Victor Emmanuel II. Austria and Prussia remained officially neutral, though several thousand Galician volunteers entered the allied ranks as private individuals. The war was fought on three fronts: the Danube, the Caucasus and the main Crimean theatre centred on Sevastopol.
people: 關鍵人物分三組。俄方：尼古拉一世拒絕任何讓步，至死不肯承認聯軍的行動合法，臨終仍把克里米亞的敗局歸咎於將領；亞歷山大二世即位後設委員會追究責任，並以此為改革鋪路；沃羅佐夫元帥在塞城以層層環形壘壕與反擊據點拖延聯軍；維特根斯坦公爵與康斯坦丁大公相繼主持多瑙河戰線；納希莫夫上將在辛諾佩海戰取勝後於慶功宴上中彈，翌日即一八五三年十二月一日傷重不治。聯軍方：拿破崙三世把戰爭當做法國重拾歐洲地位的工程；帕累托-布律埃爾上將率分艦隊強行進入黑海，維護英法的海上交通線；拉格倫公爵以五十七歲之齡任克里米亞英軍總司令，因屢遭挫折與傷病於一八五五年返英；麥克馬洪元帥同年三月接任聯軍最高指揮，帶領法軍攻佔馬拉霍夫壘；法軍上尉聖西爾在塞城觀察哨連續監視敵陣，被稱為戰爭之眼。另有撒丁的拉·馬爾莫拉元帥與加富爾，以及南丁格爾率護士團整頓斯庫塔里與巴拉克拉瓦的野戰醫院，把傷兵救護與後勤衛生制度化，間接催生紅十字會運動。
peopleEn: The decisive figures fall into three groups. On the Russian side Nicholas I refused every concession and never acknowledged that the allied action was legal; he died still blaming his generals for the failure in the Crimea. Alexander II set up a commission of inquiry once he came to the throne and used the defeat as a pretext for reform. Field Marshal Vorontsov defended Sevastopol with concentric lines of trench and counter-attack positions designed to slow the allies down. Prince Wittgenstein and then Grand Duke Konstantin commanded the Danube front in turn. Admiral Nakhimov was mortally wounded at a Victory celebration after the battle of Sinop and died of his wounds on 1 December 1853. Among the allies, Napoleon III treated the war as a means of restoring France to its place in Europe. Admiral de Parseval-Parseval forced his division into the Black Sea and kept the allied sea communications open. Lord Raglan, aged fifty-seven, was the British commander in chief in the Crimea and went home in 1855 worn down by setbacks and illness. Marshal MacMahon took over as supreme commander of the allied forces in March of the same year and led the French assault that carried the Malakoff. Captain Émile Perrin of the French army kept an observation post before Sevastopol and watched the Russian positions day and night, earning the name of the eye of the war. There were also the Sardinian commander Alfonso La Marmora and Cavour in the south, and Florence Nightingale, who took a party of nurses to reorganise the field hospitals at Scutari and Balaclava, turning the care of the wounded and the hygiene of the camps into a system and thereby helping to bring the Red Cross movement into being.
kits: 本卡線膛砲是一八五〇年代德意志諸邦在前普魯士主導下完成的前裝線膛野戰砲。膛線令彈丸旋轉，射程與精度都勝過舊式滑膛炮，克里米亞各方都大量裝備：英軍有惠特沃斯六磅線膛砲與阿姆斯特朗研製的後膛砲，法軍有六十八磅與八十磅線膛野戰砲及攻城砲，俄軍亦自製同類線膛砲。攻城方面，聯軍以二十四磅與三十二磅攻城砲組成砲壘，用平行壘壕與折線接近壕溝逐段前進，並以地雷與坑道爆破牆體；法軍莫爾尼上校推廣的楔形支撐法，用支架頂住牆身，爆破後支架被壓入裂縫，避免碎石堵塞通路。運輸與通信是這場戰爭的新事物：巴拉克拉瓦到塞城圍城線鋪設約八英里窄軌蒸汽鐵路，是戰爭史上第一條用於前線補給的鐵路；英國海軍部於一八五五年敷設海底電纜，把塞城與倫敦接通，十二月第一批電報抵達倫敦。海上則有法國的蒸汽浮動砲壘，於一八五五年十月十五日在基爾尼炮擊俄軍岸防，是日後裝甲艦的先驅。步兵方面，法國米涅式步槍與英國改裝的貝卡式步槍配恩菲爾德刺刀；騎兵有英軍輕騎旅與重騎旅、俄國哥薩克與法國胸甲騎兵。
kitsEn: The card shows a muzzle-loading rifled field gun of the type the German states, with Prussia in the lead, completed in the 1850s. Rifling spins the projectile, which gives both longer range and better accuracy than the old smooth-bore pieces, and every side in the Crimea equipped itself lavishly with them: Britain fielded the Whitworth six-pounder and Armstrong's new breech-loading gun, France used sixty-eight and eighty-pounder rifled field and siege guns, and Russia built rifled pieces of its own. For the siege the allies grouped twenty-four and thirty-two-pounder siege guns into batteries, drove their approaches by parallels and zigzag trenches, and undermined the walls with mines and galleries; the French colonel Morel popularised a ruching system in which props held the wall up, so that when the charge went off the props were driven into the crack and the debris could not plug the gallery. Transport and communications were the novelties of the war: a narrow-gauge steam railway of about eight miles ran from Balaclava to the siege lines, the first railway ever laid to supply a front, and the British Admiralty laid a submarine cable in 1855 that linked Sevastopol to London, the first dispatches reaching London that December. At sea France used steam floating batteries which shelled the Russian shore positions at Kinburn on 15 October 1855, a direct ancestor of the armoured warship. On foot the French Minié rifle and the British adapted Baker rifle were issued with bayonets for the Enfield; in the saddle there were the British light and heavy brigades, the Russian Cossacks and the French cuirassiers.
tactics: 聯軍的戰術核心是封鎖加掘壕。一八五四年九月十四日聯軍自葉夫帕托里亞登陸，俄軍放棄南克里米亞，聯軍占領巴拉克拉瓦與卡查山，切斷塞城陸路補給；英軍負責北岸防線，法軍與鄂軍負責南岸，兩面合圍。九月廿日阿爾馬河會戰，聯軍以正面強攻換取側翼突破，傷亡慘重。圍城之後，聯軍不急於強攻，而是沿塞城城牆挖平行壘壕，以折線接近壕溝逐段推進，砲兵用遠程攻城砲壓制堡壘，工程兵在地雷與坑道上下工夫；一八五四年六月、八月與十一月的三次強攻雷丹、馬梅隆與馬拉霍夫皆被挫敗。真正的破局來自一八五五年夏秋：俄軍六月八日奇襲薩彭納嶺得手，聯軍隨即趕挖壘壕，趕在俄軍之前切斷其射界；九月二日連環地雷摧毀俄軍數道壘壕，九月八日法軍以工兵突進攻佔馬拉霍夫壘，同日英軍奪取雷丹，九月九日聯軍進入塞城。聯軍最大弱點是騎兵不足，偵察與掩護砲兵都要靠步兵頂上，加上冬季衣物不足，後勤與病患造成的損失遠超會戰。
tacticsEn: The allied method was to blockade and to dig. The expedition landed at Eupatoria on 14 September 1854; the Russians evacuated southern Crimea, and the allies seized Balaclava and the Chernaya heights, cutting the land supply of Sevastopol. The British took the north side of the city, the French and the Ottomans the south, and the two wings closed in together. At the Alma on 20 September the allies bought a flanking breakthrough with frontal losses that were extremely heavy. Once the siege was established they did not rush the place. They drove parallels along the city wall, advanced by zigzag trenches, brought up heavy siege guns to silence the redoubts and put the engineers to work with mines and galleries; the assaults of the Redan, the Mamelon and the Malakoff in June, August and November 1854 were all thrown back. The breakthrough came in the summer and autumn of 1855. The Russian surprise attack on the Sapernaya Heights on 8 June forced the allies to dig faster, and by cutting the Russian line of fire in advance they stole the initiative; on 2 September a chain of mines blew up several Russian trenches, on 8 September the French sappers carried the Malakoff and the British took the Redan the same day, and on 9 September the allies entered the city. Their gravest weakness was a shortage of cavalry, so reconnaissance and the covering of the artillery had to be done by infantry on foot; added to a winter in which clothing was insufficient, the losses from sickness and supply were far greater than those of the fighting.
data: 可核對的數字集中在幾個節點。時間上：一八五三年二月俄軍越過普魯特河，十月四日鄂圖曼宣戰，十月三十日俄羅斯宣戰；一八五四年九月十四日聯軍登陸，九月二十日阿爾馬河會戰，十月二十五日巴拉克拉瓦會戰，十一月五日因克曼會戰；一八五五年九月八日馬拉霍夫壘失守，圍城自一八五四年十月十七日算起歷時三百四十九日；一八五六年三月三十日簽訂巴黎條約。兵力上，阿爾馬河會戰時聯軍約六萬人，其中英軍二萬二千餘、法軍二萬一千餘，俄軍約三萬五千；到一八五五年聯軍在克里米亞增至約十二萬，含撒丁軍約一萬五千與奧地利志願者，俄軍在克里米亞最多時約十萬人，另在多瑙河與高加索方向分兵。傷亡上，英軍陣亡約二千六百，法軍陣亡約四千上下，撒丁軍陣亡約一千二百餘，鄂軍與俄軍各以萬計，但缺乏可核對的逐項統計；一八五四年冬季的病患以萬計，遠多於會戰傷亡。辛諾佩海戰中俄國黑海分艦隊十餘艘戰艦多數被擊毀或俘獲，英法只損失數艘。技術數字上，巴拉克拉瓦至圍城線的窄軌鐵路約八英里，電纜自黑海經維也納至倫敦的總長在千公里以上。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked cluster around a few points. On timing: Russian troops crossed the Prut in February 1853; the Ottomans declared war on 4 October and Russia answered on 30 October; the allies landed on 14 September 1854, fought the Alma on 20 September, Balaclava on 25 October and Inkerman on 5 November; the Malakoff fell on 8 September 1855; the siege, counted from 17 October 1854, ran for three hundred and forty-nine days; and the Treaty of Paris was signed on 30 March 1856. On strength: at the Alma the allies had about sixty thousand men, of whom over twenty-two thousand were British and twenty-one thousand French, against roughly thirty-five thousand Russians; by 1855 the allied force in the Crimea had grown to about one hundred and twenty thousand, including some fifteen thousand Sardinians and the Austrian volunteers, while the Russian force in the Crimea reached roughly one hundred thousand at its highest, with further troops committed on the Danube and in the Caucasus. On losses: about two thousand six hundred British dead, around four thousand French, and rather more than twelve hundred Sardinians; the Ottoman and Russian totals run into the tens of thousands but there is no reliable breakdown; the sickness of the winter of 1854 ran to tens of thousands of men, far more than the casualties of the fighting. At Sinop the greater part of the Russian Black Sea division, a dozen or more sailing ships, was destroyed or captured, while the allies lost only a handful of vessels. On the technical side: the narrow-gauge line from Balaclava to the siege lines ran about eight miles, and the cable from the Black Sea to London by way of Vienna exceeded a thousand kilometres in total.
cause: 起因是東方問題同宗教權利爭端交織而成。俄國自十八世紀起主張保護鄂圖曼境內的東正教臣民，尤其看重君士坦丁堡牧首區的權力，並要求重新談判一八四九年的君士坦丁堡協議；一八五三年六月耶路撒冷聖地的聖墓教堂與伯利恆拉丁修道院使用權爭端爆發，法國要求俄國尊重天主教在聖地的既有權利，法國外相一八五三年十二月的照會把這件事推到歐洲輿論前台。直接導火線是駐多瑙河公國的鄂圖曼軍與俄軍的摩擦：一八五三年二月俄軍師團越過普魯特河進入摩爾多瓦，隨後又開入瓦拉幾亞，尼古拉一世於六月發表宣言，主張保護鄂圖曼的基督教臣民，十月雙方互相宣戰。聯盟介入各有算盤：英國怕俄國控制黑海與多瑙河、威脅通往印度的航路，也要維持歐洲均勢；法國要趁機削弱俄國、恢復對鄂圖曼的影響力，並用聯盟捆住奧地利。更遠的背景是一八四八年革命之後歐洲的緊張局勢，以及一八五〇年倫敦會議勉強維持的秩序。
causeEn: The outbreak was the product of the Eastern Question tangled up with a quarrel over religious rights. Since the eighteenth century Russia had claimed the right to protect the Orthodox subjects of the Ottoman Empire, and in particular the standing of the Patriarchate in Constantinople, and it demanded a renegotiation of the Convention of Constantinople of 1849. In June 1853 a dispute flared over the use of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre and the Latin convent at Bethlehem, and France insisted that Russia respect the established rights of the Catholics in the Holy Land; the note handed in by the French foreign minister in December 1853 carried the question to the front of European opinion. The immediate spark was friction between the Ottoman and Russian troops stationed in the Danubian Principalities: in February 1853 a Russian division crossed the Prut into Moldavia and then advanced into Wallachia, and in June Nicholas I issued a manifesto claiming the right to protect the Christian subjects of the Ottoman Empire, with both sides declaring war in October. Each ally came for its own reasons. Britain feared Russian control of the Black Sea and the Danube, the threat to the sea road to India, and the collapse of the European balance of power. France wanted to weaken Russia, to recover its old influence at Constantinople, and to tie Austria down in a coalition. Further back lay the tension in Europe after the revolutions of 1848 and the uneasy order propped up by the London conference of 1850.
impact: 影響橫跨軍事、外交與制度三層。軍事上，塞城陷落打開黑海門戶，克里米亞成為俄國南方腹地與英法土耳其航線之間的瓶頸，此後一百多年仍是歐洲強權角力的場所，直到一八七一年倫敦條約塞城才由英軍交還。技術上，蒸汽鐵路、電報、浮動砲壘與裝甲艦、線膛砲與後膛砲在同一場戰爭裡全部投入使用，各國陸軍此後重砲兵與工程兵的分量，砲兵第一次能在射程與曲射上壓過步兵，野戰砲的樣式自此全面改寫。外交上，一八五六年巴黎條約建立三項長久制度：黑海中立化、俄國放棄干預鄂圖曼內政、多瑙河公國由歐洲列強保證獨立；奧地利被排除在歐洲事務的核心之外，此後在歐洲的處境更為孤立。制度上，克里米亞的野戰醫療改革直接催生一八六三年國際紅十字委員會與一八六四年日內瓦公約，傷兵救護自此有了國際法的地位。俄國方面，敗局被視為改革必要性的證據，農奴解放與一八六〇年代各項改革都在這一陰影下推進。
impactEn: The consequences run across three layers, military, diplomatic and institutional. Militarily, the fall of Sevastopol opened the door to the Black Sea and left Crimea as the bottle neck between the southern flank of Russia and the Anglo-French route to Turkey, a ground the European powers kept contesting for more than a century until the city was handed back to Russia by the London treaty of 1871. Technically, the steam railway, the telegraph, the floating battery and the armoured ship, the rifled and the breech-loading gun all saw active service inside a single war, and from then on every army weighted its artillery and its engineers accordingly, because for the first time the gunner could outrange and outcurve the infantry and the field piece was rewritten in every detail. Diplomatically, the Treaty of Paris of 1856 set up three durable arrangements: the neutralisation of the Black Sea, the renunciation by Russia of any right to interfere in the internal affairs of the Ottoman Empire, and the independence of the Danubian Principalities guaranteed by the European powers; Austria was shut out of the substantive business of Europe and found itself more isolated there afterwards. Institutionally, the medical reform of the Crimean war led directly to the International Committee of the Red Cross in 1863 and the Geneva Convention of 1864, which placed the care of the wounded under international law. In Russia the defeat was taken as proof that reform was unavoidable, and the emancipation of the serfs and the reforms of the 1860s were all carried out in its shadow.
result: 結局是聯盟的戰術勝利與俄國的戰略退讓。塞城圍城歷時三百四十九日，一八五五年九月八日法軍工兵在馬拉霍夫壘的突破決定戰局，同日英軍攻佔雷丹，九月九日聯軍進入塞城；聯軍隨後推進至葉夫帕托里亞，俄軍放棄南克里米亞與多瑙河公國，同年十二月俄軍亦放棄對卡爾斯的圍困。一八五六年三月三十日的巴黎條約規定：俄國歸還多瑙河公國、承認黑海中立化、不得在黑海保有軍艦、不得干預鄂圖曼內政；條約在巴黎會議上簽訂，奧地利被排除在核心磋商之外。但勝利並不徹底：俄軍主力完整撤出克里米亞，國家財政與軍力未受致命打擊，東方問題並未解決，一八五七年俄國重新施壓，克里米亞的體系維持到第一次世界大戰。聯軍內部則留下裂痕：英法對塞城的管理權與克里米亞的收益分配從未談妥，奧地利更被拒於門外，這些都成為下一輪歐洲外交的伏線。
resultEn: The outcome was a tactical victory for the coalition and a strategic retreat by Russia. The siege of Sevastopol ran for three hundred and forty-nine days; on 8 September 1855 the French sappers broke through on the Malakoff and the British took the Redan the same day, and on 9 September the allies entered the city. The allies then pushed forward to Eupatoria, the Russians gave up southern Crimea and the Danubian Principalities, and in December the same year the siege of Kars was lifted. The Treaty of Paris of 30 March 1856 laid down that Russia should restore the Danubian Principalities, acknowledge the neutralisation of the Black Sea, keep no warships on it, and renounce any interference in the internal affairs of the Ottoman Empire; it was signed at the congress of Paris, with Austria excluded from the substantive deliberations. Even so the victory was not thorough. The bulk of the Russian army left Crimea intact, the finances and the military capacity of the country were not fatally damaged, and the Eastern Question was not answered: Russia resumed its pressure in 1857, and the Crimean system stood until the First World War. Cracks were left inside the coalition as well. Britain and France never settled their claims to administer Sevastopol or to divide the profits of the peninsula, and Austria was kept outside the door; all of this became part of the groundwork of the next round of European diplomacy.
